deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page in the 1983–84 'système de pseudo-droites' dossier. It has no continuous text, only figures and formulas. Several threads can be read off it.

(1) Top left: a coloured grid figure in red, yellow-green, brown and dashed lines. It continues the previous page's local models of the modified complex near the exceptional pseudo-lines D_i. The previous page discussed tubular neighbourhoods of the D_i in \tilde X, the 'faces exceptionnelles' and the rectification of the system Σ.

(2) Top right: two green 'arch' polygons whose boundary vertices are marked, some in light green. The caption reads roughly '#α ≥ 2 sommets mis en vert clair'. These look like case distinctions for an exceptional face adjacent to a boundary, with at least two vertices of a certain kind. The second arch is the same face redrawn with straightened (rectified) edges, as in the 'rectification' of the previous page.

(3) Centre: the data of a pseudo-line structure, written as a tuple (\mathcal X, K, (δ_s)_s, (ν_s), (γ_s)). Here \mathcal X is a surface and K a cell decomposition (or the union of the pseudo-lines). For each vertex s there are local data; ν_s is plausibly the order (valence) of the vertex s, which the next page uses as Σ_s ν_s = 4 s_0.

(4) The main thread is orientation bookkeeping on the surface \mathcal X at a crossing x = (a,a') of two pseudo-lines D, D'.
- ω_D denotes the orientation sheaf/torsor of the curve D, and ρ_D the orientation of its normal bundle in \mathcal X.
- At a transversal crossing, T_x\mathcal X = T_xD ⊕ T_xD', so the normal line of D is the tangent line of D'. This gives canonically ρ_D ≃ ω_{D'} and ρ_{D'} ≃ ω_D (both written twice on the page).
- The local orientation of \mathcal X at x is then ω_X ≃ ω_D ∧ ω_{D'} ≃ ρ_{D'} ∧ ω_{D'} ≃ ρ_D ∧ ω_D, up to the order of factors.
- Because ω_D ∧ ω_{D'} changes sign when the factors are swapped, Grothendieck writes ω_D ∧ ω_{D'} ∧ {D,D'}. That is, he tensors with the orientation torsor of the 2-element set {D,D'}, which makes the expression independent of the ordering. The same is done for the pair (D',D'').
- The sketches show a point a on D being transported along a path to a' on D', with frames carried along. This compares ω(D) at different points and relates ω(D) to the global ω(\mathcal X,D). The transport is labelled 'rnd α' (perhaps 'ind α' or 'mod α') and is combined with a sign β through the points Pt(D') of D meeting D'.
- The annotation 'α = −1' records nontrivial monodromy of the orientation along a pseudo-line. This is the Möbius (one-sided) behaviour of a pseudo-line in a projective-plane-like surface.
- The footnote '*) N pair, α ≠ β, ...' records a parity phenomenon: the sign obtained depends on whether the number N of crossings or lines is even.

(5) Bottom: an orthogonal pair of arrows (a local frame) and a crossing D, D' at x = (a,a'), restating the identifications ρ_D ≃ ω_{D'}, ρ_{D'} ≃ ω_D, and ρ_D ∧ ω_{D'}, ρ_{D'} ∧ ω_D.

Purpose: to control orientations, and orientability and genus, of the surface (or double cover) built from a pseudo-line system. The next page computes, for a cell structure with 4-valent vertices, s_1 = 2s_0 and χ = s_2 − s_0, so g = 1 + s_0 − s_2. Its vertices are pairs (D,a), and the count is 2n(n−1) in the 'stable' (simple) case.
errors: No outright errors are visible. The identifications ρ_D ≃ ω_{D'} at a transversal crossing are correct canonically, but only as local identifications at that point. Globally they hold only up to the transport sign, which is exactly what α, β track.
'ω_D ∧ ω_{D'}' without the {D,D'} factor depends on the ordering. Grothendieck himself corrects for this by adding ∧{D,D'}.

ideas.what: At a transversal crossing of two curves on a surface, the normal orientation of one equals the tangent orientation of the other, and the surface orientation is the wedge of the two tangent orientations.
ideas.modern_name: orientation torsors / orientation sheaves; normal bundle identification at transversal intersections

ideas.what: Making the wedge ω_D∧ω_{D'} independent of ordering by tensoring with the orientation torsor of the unordered pair {D,D'}.
ideas.modern_name: sign/orientation torsor of a finite set (determinant of a permutation representation)

ideas.what: Orientation monodromy α = −1 along a pseudo-line (one-sidedness), with a parity condition on N relating α and β.
ideas.modern_name: first Stiefel–Whitney class / w_1 of the normal bundle of a pseudo-line in RP^2-like surfaces

ideas.what: Data tuple (X, K, (δ_s), (ν_s), (γ_s)) encoding a pseudo-line system as a cell complex with vertex data.
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial encoding of pseudo-line arrangements (wiring diagrams / oriented matroids of rank 3)

deep.surprise_reason: A working sheet of figures and local orientation bookkeeping for pseudo-line systems. The identifications are routine, and no finished result or new connection is stated on this page.
transcription_corrections: The tuple is likely '(\mathcal X, K, (δ_s)_s, (ν_s), (γ_s))' rather than repeating (γ_s) twice; the next page uses ν_s for vertex orders.
The top caption reads approximately '#α ≥ 2 som[mets] mis [en] verts clair[s]'.
The right-hand formula is 'ρ_D ∧ ω_{D'}' (not ρ_{D'} ∧ ω_{D'}) in its first occurrence near the top right.
The label on the bottom crossing is '(a,a') = x', the crossing point of D and D'.
'comb. p_s' is probably 'comb. β' (the arrow from ω(D) labelled with β).
